findings.quote: The HRA balances are currently forecast to diminish from £51.5m to £4.6m by 31 March 2030, however it must be noted that there is likely to be slippage within the Capital Programme which will affect this forecast.

findings.paper_title: Ashfield DC Annual Auditors Report 24-25 to issue
findings.headline: Audit Committee has shown no improvement in rigour or challenge despite repeated prior warnings
findings.detail: The auditor, LGA Peer Challenge (2023), and Internal Audit all identified weak challenge from the Audit Committee. Despite an improvement plan developed in 2025, the auditor observed no improvement in challenge throughout 2024/25 and into September 2025, confirming this as a significant governance weakness that leaves the council exposed to unchecked risk.
findings.matters: An ineffective audit committee means the council's executive faces minimal scrutiny. Combined with the other governance failures documented here (ledger implementation, unmitigated budget gaps), weak committee challenge leaves systemic risks unaddressed.
findings.figures: Issue flagged since 2023 with no improvement observed
findings.quote: Based on our attendance throughout 2024/25, in our view, there has been no improvement in the level of challenge and this sustained level of under performance is evidence of a significant weakness in the Council's governance arrangements for effective challenge from audit committee.

findings.paper_title: Ashfield DC Annual Auditors Report 24-25 to issue
findings.headline: Council froze council tax in 2025/26 despite presenting an unmitigated £18m funding gap
findings.detail: The council applied a 2.94% council tax increase in 2024/25 to support sustainability but then froze council tax in 2025/26 despite facing an £18m medium-term funding gap. This limits income growth and compounds future pressures at precisely the moment when financial resilience is most needed.
findings.matters: A council tax freeze during a financial crisis is unusual and suggests either political constraint or unrealistic assumptions about other funding sources. It narrows the council's options for closing the funding gap.
findings.figures: 2.94% council tax increase in 2024/25; 0% (freeze) in 2025/26
findings.quote: Council Tax assumptions differ from the 2024/25 MTFP: a 2.94% increase was applied in 2024/25, but 2025/26 includes a freeze, limiting income growth and compounding future pressures. This decision was made whilst presented with an unmitigated funding gap of £18m.

findings.paper_title: Ashfield DC Annual Auditors Report 24-25 to issue
findings.headline: 2025/26 budget dependent on drawing £4.2m from reserves to balance despite unresolved systemic issues
findings.detail: The council shifted from a balanced 2024/25 budget (no reserve drawdown) to a 2025/26 budget requiring £2.209m from general reserve and £2.044m from earmarked reserves. This occurs while facing an £18m medium-term gap and with reserves projected to fall to around £8m if current trajectory continues. The freeze on council tax (despite facing a funding crisis) compounds the income pressure.
findings.matters: Escalating reserve dependency signals unsustainable financial management. A fall to £8m in useable reserves leaves the council with minimal financial buffer for volatility or service demands.
findings.figures: £2.209m general reserve drawdown; £2.044m earmarked reserve drawdown in 2025/26; total general and earmarked reserves of £26.5m reduced to approximately £8m forecast if current plan continues
findings.quote: Where the 2024/25 budget was balanced without drawing on the General Reserve, the 2025/26 budget requires £2.209m from the General Reserve and £2.044m from earmarked reserves to achieve balance. This reliance on reserves highlights increasing financial pressure and a shift away from structural balance.

findings.paper_title: Ashfield DC Annual Auditors Report 24-25 to issue
findings.headline: New financial ledger system implementation has failed to provide reliable financial data eight months after go-live
findings.detail: The new ledger went live in August 2024 but without documented governance, project plan, or data migration assurance. It has caused persistent operational failures: delayed invoice payments, broken authorization processes, inability to complete reconciliations, and forced the council to pay suppliers by credit card (~£60k/month) as a workaround—a control environment that increases fraud risk. The 2024/25 financial statements remain unpublished as a result (five months past deadline as of late November 2025).
findings.matters: If the council cannot reliably track its own transactions or produce timely accounts, it cannot manage its finances effectively. The use of credit cards to bypass normal controls is a material control weakness. This undermines confidence in any financial reporting and budget setting.
findings.figures: ~£60,000 per month in credit card payments; 2024/25 accounts unpublished at 27 November 2025 (five months after statutory deadline of 30 June 2025)
findings.quote: the Council had to make payments to suppliers using Credit Cards at around £60,000 per month. This creates a heightened risk of fraud.

findings.paper_title: Ashfield DC Annual Auditors Report 24-25 to issue
findings.headline: Unmitigated cumulative funding gap of £18m in 2026/27 and 2027/28 with no credible closure plan
findings.detail: The Council approved a Medium-Term Financial Strategy showing a cumulative funding gap of £18m over two years with no plan to bridge it other than a £0.6m savings plan. At the council's current savings rate of 2.2% of total spend (£568k from £22.017m budget), closing this gap would take approximately 37 years. A September 2025 update narrowed the gap to £10.2m but still leaves a material deficit.
findings.matters: A multi-year funding gap of this scale with inadequate savings plans indicates the council will either face service reductions or continued material reserve depletion. This is a core financial sustainability risk.
findings.figures: £18m cumulative gap 2026/27 and 2027/28; £0.6m savings plan identified; 2.2% savings rate against total spend of £22.017m; reduced to £10.2m gap in September 2025 update
findings.quote: The Council also accepted a Medium-Term Financial Strategy that had a cumulative funding gap of £18m in 2026/27 and 2027/28 and, other than a £0.6m savings plan in 2025/26, there was no plan to bridge this budget gap, which, if realized, would have a significant impact on the Council's useable revenue reserves.

findings.paper_title: Ashfield DC Annual Auditors Report 24-25 to issue
findings.headline: Auditor has disclaimed opinion on financial statements for year ended 31 March 2025
findings.detail: The auditor cannot express an opinion that the financial statements are true and fair. This prevents any reliance on the published accounts. The disclaimer follows delays in producing the 2024/25 accounts, which remained unpublished at the time of this report (27 November 2025), months after the statutory deadline.
findings.matters: A disclaimed opinion means no independent verification that the council's financial position is accurately stated. This is a material risk for any lender assessing creditworthiness or for the council's own financial planning.
findings.figures: 2024/25 financial statements disclaimed
findings.quote: Our opinion on the financial statements will be disclaimed.
